avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The city buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional lots. Boroughs are adding their own means: money from park funds, machinery rental, blue-collar worker teams. Variances also set out tree planting rules in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and to Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the chalet in parc Pratt and redeveloping its surroundings, including planting vegetation, partly financed by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by no later than December 31, 2026, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs rented vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, the contract for cleaning sidewalks in the four private snow removal sectors was awarded for $271,979.11, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie entrusted companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger and Place des Montréalaises, as well as square Dorchester, place du Canada, îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris and square Chaboillez. The borough also extended by one year the snow removal of the Quartier des Spectacles, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027.

City council and the executive committee extended turnkey snow removal contracts by twelve months in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, as well as towing contracts, equipment rentals with operator and snow removal of a municipal parking lot. Boroughs did the same for their own vehicle rentals.

aSurveiller.texte: The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
Snow removal for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and starting work on its drinking water and sewer networks, in several boroughs and on main pipes. It is also continuing the wastewater disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and paying for the day-to-day operation of this plant. Boroughs are taking charge of replacing lead water service connections, including the portion located on private land.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, without digging trenches, and to redo the roadway on various streets in many boroughs. These contracts include the replacement of lead water service connections on both the public side and the private side.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections on private land
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering to have city council take charge of replacing lead service connections located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the property owners concerned [CA26 22 0034].

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild water pipes and infrastructure along rue Guy and on rue De Champlain, and is adding amounts to the contracts for rue Saint-Antoine Ouest and rue de la Cathédrale. On rue De Champlain, the work site replaces a 1,200 mm pipe installed in 1927 [CG26 0332].

The City is renewing or awarding contracts to operate the wastewater treatment plant: process control system, chemicals, residue landfilling, housekeeping, upgrading of sludge incinerators and mechanical work. The mechanical work aims notably to recondition screens damaged during intense rainfalls [CG26 0543].

aSurveiller.texte: Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026, then of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Adoption expected on October 19, 2026 of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.
Rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord to be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale pipe pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Work site on rue Guy expected to continue until December 2027; commissioning of the ozone plant expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park by phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward with several projects at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is launching the construction of a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, replacing electrical equipment at the site, renewing park maintenance, and redeveloping rue De Louvain near the park. It is also asking the Québec government for money for a cycling and pedestrian link.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail crossing the park, including a footbridge about 150 metres long, and assistance of up to $2,000,000 [CG26 0121].

The City approves the construction of a greenhouse complex near the composting platform, then hands the project over to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The borough then awards a contract for $499,865.92, taxes included, to supply and install two greenhouses, with $74,979.88 in contingencies [CA26 14 0163].

The City awards a contract for $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, with $163,754.01 in contingencies. The work involves a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and an automated system to manage biogas capture [CG26 0223].

The borough awards a contract of up to $8,199,514.82, taxes included, to redevelop rue De Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a total authorized expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings [CA26 14 0076].

The City awards two companies the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028. It also extends the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium by six months, for an additional $193,215.49, taxes included [CG26 0521].

The City extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the complex by five months, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included; the compost is used in part to landscape the park [CG26 0320]. In October, the borough authorizes the submission of a funding request to the Véloce III program for the bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is submitting its request, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The extended snow removal contract covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, additional mortar, sod and a degraded culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The submission involves no expense; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. The 2025 report filed shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, representing 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Rebuilding of the chemin Senneville culvert
etapes.texte: A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expense reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and 9232-3914 Québec inc. the housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expense of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting-up of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose the project funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fitting-up work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to guide people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes over the litigation concerning the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and housing projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM, transfers or purchases land for social housing, and pays grants to organizations building affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.titre: Budgets of the SHDM and the OMHM
etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units [CM26 0114]. City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the 2026 budget of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households [CG26 0024].

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half of the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre piece of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost [CG26 0042]. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square-metre piece of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where the cooperative must build 26 housing units [CG26 0062].

The City adds $877,312 to its support for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve [CG26 0171]. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project [CG26 0178].

etapes.titre: Land purchase and right of first refusal
etapes.texte: The City buys, for $9,293,113 plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre piece of land near rues Chatham and William, in the Sud-Ouest, for social housing purposes [CG26 0286]. It removes from the right of first refusal for social housing lots in Ville-Marie and the Sud-Ouest that had been subject to it since 2020 [CG26 0292].

The City pays $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel for 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus [CG26 0372] and $13,151,528 to Immobilier collectif – Point commun for 395 housing units in Pointe-Saint-Charles [CG26 0559]. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build 72 housing units on 2e Avenue [CE26 1028], and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a policy to reimburse 50% of permit fees for eligible projects [CA26 170209].

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 housing units at Technopôle Angus by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Delivery of the SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue in May 2028.
Occupancy of the 395-unit building in Pointe-Saint-Charles in February 2030.
Integration of the fee exemption into the 2027 local fee schedule by-law in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal lands in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: City council extended the lease of a 2,787 square metre lot to the Société de transport de Montréal, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent, for a total rent of $49,293. It also extended the lease of a neighbouring 836 square metre lot to an app-based parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités," because the first residential project is under construction and addresses need to be assigned. The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Contract for the street and soils
etapes.texte: The City awarded Charex inc. the construction of a 610-metre street with sewer, waterworks, lighting and underground electrical network, for $10,311,940.25 including taxes, and a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the rehabilitation of the soils of the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net through the environmental liability reserve.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It then launched a draft by-law allowing, on part of the municipal lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, a height limit of 73 metres and a floor area ratio of 6.

etapes.titre: Redevelopment of rue de Louvain Est
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes and a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. In October, it authorized the filing of a financial assistance application to the ministère des Transports for the bike lane and sidewalks of this section.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Laboratoire sur l'agriculture urbaine runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027; the Ville en vert vegetable garden is loaned until December 31, 2027.
Îlot 84 could occupy the Esplanade lot from April 1 to October 31, 2027.
Work on rue de Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks and curbs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
Four other public places in the eco-district remain to be named before the completion of the development, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for citizens. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also submitting the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Purchase of bins and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council concludes agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to citizens in the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program lending reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations at neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration extends the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract of $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, entrusts two firms with studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages discharge authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program lending dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the discharge authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026, to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an extra delay from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and the public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline postponed to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not entail any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and leisure centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transition nursery. Each lease provides for a token rent, and the organizations pay for development, upkeep and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal subsidy is conditional on completing the infrastructure by 2031; the credits from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora and April 30, 2028 for the transition nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.

etapes.titre: Plans and studies before the work
etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil and environmental studies of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, built on a former dump.

The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract for the restoration of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, having a culvert rebuilt at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche, and awarding contracts for snow removal and the felling of ash trees and dying trees. It is adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments and submitting Cap-Saint-Jacques's candidacy for Urban Night Sky Place designation.

The City and the boroughs are adding funds or shifting budgets for work already underway: monitoring of parc du Bassin-à-Bois, parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray, plans for parc Percy-Walters, and museography for parc des Sœurs de Sainte-Anne in Lachine.

City council is removing an 810.2 m² street section from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, in Le Sud-Ouest. Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is requesting the same for a 75.2 m² strip of laneway that crosses parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: City council must rule on October 19, 2026 on the removal of the laneway strip from parc Le Prévost, after it goes before the executive committee on October 7, 2026.
For the artwork at parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, and installation in 2028.
The Grand parc de l'Ouest snow removal contract covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027, after the warranty year.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques candidacy: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, and site compliance work in April 2032.
Work on parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, is expected to be completed in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid out $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted by-laws closing streets and authorizing terraces, sales, and music. Other decisions concern public squares: landscaping, a change in the status of a piece of land, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by by-law [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

etapes.titre: Money paid to commercial development corporations
etapes.texte: The boroughs pay contributions to commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre piece of land at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes the sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on the sound ambiance of the Quartier des spectacles pedestrian streets runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, that is until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting six additional months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing heights, uses and the building footprint ratio in the sector bordered by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing allowed heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the extension granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, a date set by the minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and to hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: City council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment for the SPVM between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes lending a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City awards 9415-1966 Québec inc. the contract for meals for people detained by the SPVM and extends by one year the software maintenance for the computer-aided dispatch system with Peraton International. It leases 50 parking spaces from the Société de la Place des arts, extends the lease for the training centre in Anjou and the one for neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and accepts $8,000 from Ottawa for an information campaign on sexual assaults.

etapes.titre: Ammunition, courier services and building trades
etapes.texte: The City enters into an agreement with Agence Gravel for 9 mm practice ammunition for firearms training, extends the SPVM's courier contract by one year and renews the lease for neighbourhood station 26, avenue Mountain Sights. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings, and lends a detective sergeant to the Sûreté du Québec team on the export of stolen vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day of the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the Anjou borough bought 62 tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the 10-year lease for the metro unit space of neighbourhood station 50, at 888, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the harbour patrol boat and its trailer.
March 31, 2027: end of the period covered by the grants from the ACCES Tabac, ACCES Alcool, ACCES Cannabis and ACCEF committees.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and the loan by-laws of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then sells, leases or lends it land to expand metro stations and facilities. It also signs agreements to carry out municipal work at the same time as the work on the blue line extension, and oversees metro and REM construction sites. Borough councils also adopt motions on network development.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council approves the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410, and its 2026-2035 capital works program [CG26 0022]. The City also enters into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, for a maximum of $41,944,604.63 including taxes, plus contingencies [CG26 0064].

etapes.titre: Land sold, leased and lent to the STM
etapes.texte: The City sells the STM a 364.3 m² piece of land near the Place-Saint-Henri station for $495,150 plus taxes [CG26 0348], land in Verdun for the Rielle ventilation station [CG26 0349], and commits to selling a portion of rue Jean-Brillant for a rectifier station [CG26 0375]. It also leases a parking lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville to the STM [CM26 0078], lends it a small building on rue Stinson for its drivers [CE26 1303], and signs an access agreement for a piece of land on boulevard Décarie [CA26 170103].

etapes.titre: Work entrusted to the STM and bus stops
etapes.texte: The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes [CG26 0175]. It also signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur, backing onto a metro ventilation station in Outremont [CM26 0198], while Ahuntsic-Cartierville sets up and removes bus waiting posts as part of the network overhaul [CA26 09 0020].

The urban agglomeration council approves several STM loans: metro infrastructure repairs, surface building repairs, bus priority measures, cybersecurity, extending the lifespan of the MR-73 cars and analyzing their replacement. The 2026-2035 Capital Works Program is amended each time.

The City retains Artelia Canada and Stantec Experts-conseils for the redevelopment of the blue line corridor, from Saint-Michel to Anjou, for an estimated amount of $19,070,092.68 including taxes [CG26 0564]. City council asks Québec to study keeping the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line extension [CM26 0920]; Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring projects in the East End and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, Anjou asks for the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien to be stopped, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks at bus stops.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the parking lot south of rue de Louvain begins on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Repair and expansion work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for at most two weeks during the summer 2027 holidays; bridge-tunnel work is scheduled until March 2028.
The opening of the five stations of the blue line extension is planned for 2031; the integrated municipal work is planned for 2028-2029.
The professional services agreements for the blue line corridor run from October 2026 to October 2032.

velo.titre: Bikes: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the BIXI bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI bike-sharing system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike infrastructure projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an order formalizing the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse, and imposing mandatory manoeuvres on drivers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread, among other places, on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then hired Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers used as the base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal hired Cojalac inc. for work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and Le Sud-Ouest hired Groupe Damex inc. for the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
Repairs to the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, are budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
